reason: Reviewed lifecycle hooks, the shipped skill and native-question reference, harness setup, CLI readiness, domain terms and trust boundaries. Machine approval now returns a structured local handoff before a foreground auth wait pinned to the presented invitation. The agent displays the QR then awaits the same tool handle, or resumes the exact pairing after interruption, without requiring a conversation reply from the User. Approved stores the credential and resumes setup; denied or expired stops without replacement. A network outage through the deadline preserves the pending invitation and reports unavailable, not an inferred decision. Other harness routing, ownership, notification content and acknowledgement obligations remain unchanged; no hook or approved Machine is required to wait for approval. Proof-bearing QR/link data stays local. These source changes do not establish live per-harness physical approval or publication evidence. The waiter retries transient HTTP failures as well as network errors. A late pending response never establishes expiry: only a terminal service response discards the invitation.
